Generate the tests from the approved requirements and design.

I fixed four of the five test problems, and one failure is a code bug. I haven't re-run `run_tests` since the last edit (the `SEQ-006` change), but `typecheck` is clean. The run just before it had 31 tests passing and 2 failing.

**Test fixes (each recorded with `report_test_fix`):**
- **UC-006 (six REQ-005/REQ-010 tests):** The fake item used a `highestBid` field instead of the `Item` shape's `highestBidAmount`. That caused the "amount must be a non-negative finite number" errors. I fixed the shared fixture. In the last run, `REQ-005` AC1–AC4 and `REQ-010` AC1–AC3 passed with it.
- **`SEQ-006` scenario:** It used display currency CHF on a CHF item, so no rate fetch is needed. It now uses EUR. In the last run it failed on the fetch-call assertion, which this change addresses.
- **`SEQ-004` scenario:** The fake socket had no `readyState`, which a real WebSocket always has. I added an open `readyState`, and the test passed in the last run.
- **`SEQ-005` scenario:** `AuctionCloser.tick` closes auctions due at the current time, and the test item ended in 2030. The item's end time is now in the past, and the test passed in the last run.

**Code bug (recorded with `report_code_bug`):**
- **`REQ-002` AC4 (`test/UC-003.test.ts`):** A second bid equal to the first was accepted. `BidService.placeBid` should save the new highest bid on the item through `saveItem`. It should also enforce a minimum of the highest bid plus 1.
Apply the fix for "REQ-002 AC4: Any later bid is accepted only if it is at least 1 unit of the item currency higher than the current highest bid, otherwise it is rejected." (20261122-131901-P5-1).

I fixed the bug in `src/auction-api/BidService.ts`. I haven't run the test itself, only typecheck and drift. Both are clean.

`placeBid` never recorded an accepted bid on the item. `highestBidAmount` and `highestBidderId` stayed null, so the second bid of 100 was still checked against the starting price and passed. After the bid is stored, `placeBid` now sets both fields on the item before calling `saveItem`. The next bid is then checked against the highest bid plus 1.

`Item.minimumBid()` already returned highest plus 1 when a bid exists, so I left it alone.

The one failing test, REQ-002 AC4 in `test/UC-003.test.ts`, is a code bug. I left the test unchanged and reported it. I did not run `typecheck` or `run_tests`, because I changed no files.

The test places a bid of 100 and then a second bid of 100. The criterion says a later bid must be at least 1 unit higher than the current highest bid, so the second bid should be rejected. It was accepted. The test matches the criterion, so the bid check in `BidService.placeBid` is wrong.

My proposed fix is that `placeBid` should reject any amount below the highest bid plus 1. An accepted bid should also update the item's highest bid and bidder and save the item. I could not see the implementation, so I can't say which of those is the actual cause.
Apply the fix for "REQ-002 AC4: Any later bid is accepted only if it is at least 1 unit of the item currency higher than the current highest bid, otherwise it is rejected." (20261124-095100-P5-1).

I fixed the bug in `src/auction-api/BidService.ts`. `placeBid` never recorded an accepted bid on the item, so the next bid was still checked against the starting price. A second bid of 100 passed because 100 is above the starting price of 50.

Now an accepted bid sets `item.highestBidAmount` and `item.highestBidderId` before `saveItem` runs. The existing minimum check, which already required the highest bid plus 1, now applies to every later bid.

I didn't run the test itself. `typecheck` and `detect_drift` are both clean, and I didn't run `start_app` because the change doesn't touch the wiring.
Generate the tests from the approved requirements and design.

All nine failures came from wrong tests, so I fixed the tests and reported no code bugs. Typecheck is clean. The full run passed 37 of 38 before my last edit, and the one failure was REQ-010 AC3, which I then fixed. I re-ran only `UC-006` after that, and all 8 of its tests pass.

- **`UC-002` SEQ-002:** `GET /api/items/:id` returns an `ItemView` with the item nested. The test now reads `body.item.title`.
- **`UC-004` (REQ-007 AC1, AC2 and SEQ-004):** the tests guessed a topic name `bid` that the design never defines. They now build the event through the real `BidEventPublisher` and pass its topic and payload to `EventFeedClient`.
- **`UC-006` (REQ-005 AC1, AC3, AC4, REQ-010 AC3 and SEQ-006):** the fake item used a field `highestBid`, but `Item` has `highestBidAmount`.
- **`UC-006` REQ-010 AC3:** I removed the assertion that `displayCurrency` is null on fallback. The criterion only requires that prices are shown in the item currency, with no converted prices. The null checks on the converted prices stay.

Each change is recorded with `report_test_fix`.

Add tests that pin these rules, keep every existing test:
1. AuctionCloser: constructing it with intervalMs 0, -1 or 1.5 throws; 1000 does not (design DSN-024).
2. ItemStore: after saving an item and a bid, the items.endTime and bids.placedAt columns hold ISO 8601 TEXT (typeof is 'text' in SQLite) and an item read back has the same endTime (design DSN-029).

I added two new test files, `test/DSN-024.test.ts` and `test/DSN-029.test.ts`, and left every existing test alone. Typecheck is clean and all 7 new tests pass. I ran only the new files (filter `DSN-0`), not the full suite.

- **DSN-024:** four tests. Constructing `AuctionCloser` with intervalMs 0, -1 or 1.5 throws, and 1000 does not.
- **DSN-029:** three tests against a `:memory:` database.
  - After saving an item and a bid, `typeof` of `items.endTime` is `text`. The stored value is the ISO 8601 string of the date.
  - The same holds for `bids.placedAt`.
  - An item read back through `findItem` has an `endTime` equal to the saved one.

The titles of these tests carry the design IDs (DSN-024, DSN-029), not REQ criteria. The brief's naming contract has no pattern for design rules, so I used that.

I patched the tests for the changed and added IDs. Typecheck is clean and the full run passed 57 tests, with 0 failing and 8 todo. I reported no code bugs.

- **Constructor fix:** `Item` now takes a reserve price and `ItemService.listItem` takes a sixth argument. I updated the item construction in `UC-003`, `UC-004` and `UC-005`, and in `DSN-029`, which stopped compiling.
- **UC-002 (list item):**
  - New tests cover REQ-001 AC4 and AC5 and REQ-012 AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC7.
  - REQ-012 AC7 checks that the create, view and list responses never contain the reserve amount.
  - The `SEQ-002` scenario now lists with a reserve and also checks that an unknown seller is rejected.
- **UC-004 (watch live):** I added REQ-012 AC8. A bid event carries the reserve-met state and not the reserve amount. The reserve-met check looks for the text `reserveMet` followed by `true` in the event payload. The design doesn't define the payload shape, so that name is my guess from `PublicItem.reserveMet`.
- **UC-005 (close auction):**
  - REQ-004 is now numbered AC1–AC6. I retitled the watcher test to AC5 and the no-bids test to AC6.
  - I added REQ-004 AC3 and AC4, and REQ-012 AC4 and AC5.
  - The `SEQ-005` scenario now closes an item with a reserve and checks `publishAuctionClosed`.
- **UC-006 (prices):** I added REQ-012 AC6 (reserve-met state shown, no reserve amount). The `SEQ-006` scenario checks the same.
- **UC-003 (place bid):** I only fixed the constructor. REQ-012 AC8 is covered once, in `UC-004`.

I recorded a `report_test_fix` for the retitled and changed-criterion tests: REQ-004 AC5 and AC6, and the `SEQ-005`, `SEQ-002` and `SEQ-006` scenarios.
